title: The ACT: Format & the 'Enhanced' Changes
summary: The ACT's core sections, the new composite based on English/Math/Reading, and what the enhanced-ACT changes mean for you.

chunks.heading: Three core sections, plus options
chunks.body: The ACT's **scored core is English, Mathematics and Reading**. **Science** and **Writing (an essay)** are **additional** sections. Each section is scored **1–36**, and the **Composite is the average of English, Math and Reading** (rounded), with Science reported separately if you take it.
chunks.realExample: A Composite of 30 might come from English 31, Math 28, Reading 31 — averaged and rounded. Science, if taken, appears as its own score and a STEM score, not folded into the Composite.
chunks.memoryHook: Composite = average of English, Math, Reading. Science & Writing are extras, scored separately.

chunks.heading: The 'enhanced ACT' is changing things
chunks.body: The ACT is being **updated**: the **Composite moved to the English/Math/Reading average**, **Science is becoming optional**, and the test is getting **more time per question and slightly shorter** — changes rolling out across 2025–2026. Because it's phased, **confirm what your specific test date and target colleges require**.
chunks.realExample: Some test dates/colleges still expect Science; others treat it as optional. Check your registration and each college's policy rather than assuming — the rules are mid-transition.
chunks.memoryHook: Enhanced ACT = E/M/R composite + optional Science + more time. It's phased — confirm your date.

chunks.heading: Each section 1–36
chunks.body: Every section is scored on the **1–36 ACT scale**, based on the number of correct answers converted to a scaled score. There's **no penalty for wrong answers**, so **always fill in an answer** for every question, even a guess.
chunks.realExample: With no wrong-answer penalty, a blank is a wasted chance — in the last 30 seconds, put an answer on every remaining question (a 'letter of the day' guess beats blanks).
chunks.memoryHook: 1–36 per section. No penalty — never leave a bubble blank.

chunks.heading: Pacing is the ACT's real challenge
chunks.body: The ACT is known for its **fast pace** — you have limited time per question, so **timing and momentum matter as much as knowledge**. Do a first pass answering what you know, mark the hard ones, and return with leftover time.
chunks.realExample: In Reading, don't perfect one passage while the clock runs — get the answerable questions across all passages first, then revisit tough ones. Finishing beats perfecting a few.
chunks.memoryHook: The ACT rewards pace. Answer the sure ones first; never let one question sink the section.

recall.q: Which sections make up the ACT Composite score?
recall.a: The average of English, Mathematics and Reading (each 1–36), rounded — Science and Writing are scored separately.

recall.q: What are the main 'enhanced ACT' changes?
recall.a: The Composite is now the English/Math/Reading average, Science is becoming optional (phased), and there's more time per question with a slightly shorter test.

recall.q: How is each ACT section scored?
recall.a: On a 1–36 scale, from correct answers converted to a scaled score.

recall.q: Is there a penalty for wrong answers on the ACT?
recall.a: No — so you should always put an answer for every question, even a guess.

recall.q: Why should you confirm requirements with your test date and colleges?
recall.a: The enhanced-ACT changes (composite, optional Science, timing) are rolling out in phases, so requirements vary by date and college.
